title: Ang 1168–1171: Basant begins
hook: Guru Nanak opens the spring raga
tomorrow: spring comes for everyone. why does a Guru say only for some?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ravidas closed Bhairao: what is seen will pass, so turn the longing toward the Name. That's the whole morning raga behind us, six days of it, from Guru Nanak's first line to Ravidas's last.
screen: `RAVIDAS: WHAT IS SEEN WILL PASS.` → `BHAIRAO, BEHIND US.`

segments.voice: The first warm afternoon after a long gray stretch: windows open, somebody's mowing, a bird you forgot existed starts up again. Nobody decides to feel lighter. It just happens. Turn the page from Ravidas, to ang 1168, and the Granth does the same thing. A new raga starts, Basant, the spring raga, and Guru Nanak opens it.
screen: `THE FIRST WARM AFTERNOON.` → `WINDOWS OPEN.` → `BASANT, THE SPRING RAGA.`

segments.voice: In paraphrase, Guru Nanak's first Basant hymn begins: of all the months, blessed is the one when spring comes, and stays. Blossom, my mind, remembering the Lord, always. Listen to the twist. Real spring leaves. This one is called forever spring, sadaa basant, because it isn't in the calendar. It's in the mind that remembers. Something to tell a friend tonight: in the Granth, the spring raga comes straight after the serious morning one, with no gap at all: Ravidas's last line on one page, and spring on the next. And that's a good way to look back on the week, because every hymn we read in Bhairao was about where to put the mind. Nothing outside the One. One clay, many pots. I serve the One. A wealth not knotted, not sold. A cup of milk, meant. What's seen will pass. Six lines from one morning raga, and now the spring raga picks up the same thread: blossom, remembering.
screen: `BLESSED IS THE MONTH SPRING COMES.` · `BLOSSOM, MY MIND.` · `FOREVER SPRING: NOT IN THE CALENDAR.` · `A WEEK OF BHAIRAO, LOOKING BACK.` · then, large: `SPRING.`

segments.voice: Find one living thing you can see from where you are: a plant on a shelf, a tree through the window, a weed in a crack. Look at it for this sit, and look for one thing about it that's growing. If you'd like, read ang 1168 before you begin.
Ang 1168. Where Basant begins: Guru Nanak's spring raga, and a mind told to blossom, remembering.
Spring, the Basant kind: a season the mind can carry into any month. Week done. Next week, more spring.

screen: `DAY 1589 COUNTS.` → `A WALK THROUGH THE GRANTH · 143 OF 180.` → `TOMORROW: SPRING COMES FOR EVERYONE. WHY DOES A GURU SAY ONLY FOR SOME?`
